edition: Lenny Two Screen Australian Female Voice

speech.text: You’ve unlocked all five skills! Now use them to make something of your own. Who will you make it for?
Oh, hello! Lovely to see you. What shall we chat about?
Mmm! That was scrumptious! High paws!
You did it! You earned a silly meat treat. Tap Feed Lenny and see what happens!
Nom, nom, nom!
Woohoo! Thank you for telling me! You gave it a go and that is what counts. High paws!

Oh, hello there! I’m Lenny. Hee hee! Shall we go on a little adventure?
Hello, explorer! What should I call you? Type your name or nickname, then tap Let’s play.

Your mission is The Fair-Play Puzzle. Two toys. One special crayon. What should they do? You need: Two toys, one crayon and a partner. Here is what to do. First. Pretend two toys both want the same special crayon. Ask a partner to speak for one toy. Next. Each toy explains why it wants the crayon. Listen before you suggest a plan. Then. Think of two ways to share it. Ask what each toy likes or dislikes about each plan. Finally. Choose a plan together and act it out. If one toy is unhappy, change the plan and try again. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is The Tower That Learns. Your first tower is only the beginning. Can you improve it? You need: Six paper cups or safe blocks, paper for a flag, and crayons. Here is what to do. First. Build a tower with six paper cups or safe blocks. Draw or remember your first design. Next. Make a little paper flag. Can your tower hold it while you count to ten? Then. Build again with the same pieces. Change just one thing, such as the width of the base. Finally. Test with the same flag. Compare your towers and explain what helped one stay up. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is The Kindness Detective. Find a real problem and make someone’s day a little better. You need: Someone at home who would like a small helping hand. Here is what to do. First. Ask someone at home what small thing would make their day easier. Listen without guessing. Next. Think of two ways you could help. Ask which would be most useful. Then. Do the chosen job with their permission. Ask a grown-up to help if you need it. Finally. Ask whether your help worked. Tell Lenny what you noticed and what you would do next time. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is Invent for Someone. Make something useful for someone else. What do they need? You need: A toy, paper, a towel or box, and a customer. A grown-up can help with tape. Here is what to do. First. Ask someone which toy needs a bed, a shelter or a carrying box. Listen to what it must do. Next. Draw two different ideas. Ask which one they would like you to build and why. Then. Build their choice using paper, a towel or a box. Ask a grown-up for help if you need tape. Finally. Let your customer test it with the toy. Use their feedback to change one thing, then show what improved. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is The Secret Builder. Can you build a picture in someone else’s mind? You need: Five safe objects, paper, crayons and a partner. Here is what to do. First. Choose five safe objects. One person makes a little model while the other looks away. Next. Describe your model to your partner. They draw it without looking. Use words like beside, above and between. Then. Compare the drawing with the model. Find one detail your words could explain more clearly. Finally. Swap builder and artist. Try your clearer words and see what changes. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is The Mystery Object Show. Can you make an ordinary thing sound extraordinary? You need: One safe household object and a willing audience. Here is what to do. First. Choose a safe object and imagine a new use for it. A sock could be a dragon’s sleeping bag! Next. Practise a short show. Tell your audience what it is, how it works and who would use it. Then. Give your show without naming the real object. Let your audience guess. Finally. Listen to their question. Add one detail to make your explanation clearer, then try your show again. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is Secret Island Map. Can your team find the treasure using words? You need: Paper, crayons, a small toy and a partner. Here is what to do. First. With a partner, make an island on paper. Add a start, a treasure and three obstacles. Next. Choose who gives directions first. Your partner moves a toy along the map, following your words. Then. Can you guide them to the treasure without touching an obstacle? Give one direction at a time. Finally. Swap jobs. Change any direction that was confusing, then tell each other which words helped. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is The Party Planner. Lenny has eight coins for a party. How will you spend them? You need: Paper, crayons, eight large paper coins and a partner. Here is what to do. First. Plan a pretend party for a toy. Make eight large paper coins. Next. Draw choices for snacks, games and decorations. Give each choice a price from one to three coins. Then. Pick things for your party without spending more than eight coins. Count what is left. Finally. A guest wants one more game. Decide what you could swap or remove to pay for it. Explain your choice. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is Make a Marble-Free Maze. Build a puzzle that is tricky, fair and fun. You need: Paper, crayons, one large paper ball and a tester. Here is what to do. First. Draw a maze for a large paper ball. Add a start, a finish and three tricky turns. Next. Move the ball through with one finger. Notice where it is too easy or gets stuck. Then. Change two parts of the maze. Try to make it tricky but possible. Finally. Ask someone to test it. Watch where they struggle, then improve one clue or turn. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is The Five-Coin Toy Shop. Can you make a shop your customer wants to visit? You need: Paper, crayons, five large paper coins and a customer. Here is what to do. First. Draw three things to sell. Give them prices of one, two and three paper coins. Next. Give your customer five paper coins. Explain what makes each thing worth buying. Then. Let them choose what to buy. Count the cost and how many coins they have left. Finally. Ask why they chose it. Improve one thing in your shop, then swap jobs and try again. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is Lenny’s Newsroom. A visitor has landed on Lenny’s island. Get the story! You need: A toy and a partner to play the visitor. Here is what to do. First. Choose a toy to be a visitor from a made-up planet. Ask a partner to be the visitor. Next. Think of three questions. Find out where they live, what they eat and one surprising fact. Then. Listen to the answers. Give a short news report about your visitor using all three facts. Finally. Ask the visitor if you got the facts right. Fix one detail and give your report again. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is The Paper Bridge Lab. Can one sheet of paper become a stronger bridge? You need: Two low books, one sheet of paper and three paper balls. Here is what to do. First. Put two low books a hand-width apart. Use one sheet of paper to make a bridge. Next. Test it with three paper balls. How many stay on before the bridge bends? Then. Use the same sheet to make a different bridge. Try folds or a rolled edge. Test with the same balls. Finally. Compare your tests. Choose the stronger design and explain what you changed. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is The Wrong Ending. One story. Two endings. Which will your audience choose? You need: Toys or drawing paper, and someone to hear your story. Here is what to do. First. Choose a character, a place and something the character wants. Draw them or use toys. Next. Tell a story with a beginning, a problem and an ending. Act it out for someone. Then. Now change the ending. What if your character makes a different choice? Finally. Tell both endings. Ask your listener which they prefer and why. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is The Welcome Mission. Someone new wants to play. Help them feel they belong. You need: A toy, a partner and a simple game you both know. Here is what to do. First. Imagine a toy is new to a game. Ask a partner to play the new toy. Next. Ask the newcomer what they like and what they are unsure about. Listen to the answer. Then. Change one rule or give them a useful role so they can join in. Play a short round. Finally. Ask how it felt to join. Use their answer to make your welcome even better. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Your mission is Rescue Mission. A toy is stranded! Can your team bring it home? You need: A toy, paper for a river, two cushions, a towel and a partner. Here is what to do. First. Put a toy beside a paper river on the floor. You have two cushions and a towel to make a safe route. Next. Make a rescue plan together. Each person adds an idea. Choose who plans the route and who moves the toy. Then. Try the rescue. Keep your feet on the floor and pretend the toy cannot touch the river. Finally. Swap jobs and try a better route. Tell your partner which idea made the rescue work. When you are done, come back and tap I did it.

Time for your big idea! Part 1. Your big idea. Choose a real person. Ask what would make their day more fun or easier. Decide what you want to make for them. Part 2. Make a first version. Draw two ideas. Choose one and build a small version using things at home. You choose how it works. Part 3. Test it with someone. Let your person try it. Ask what works and what could be better. Change one thing using their feedback. Part 4. Showtime!. Show your invention to someone. Explain who it helps, how it works and what you changed after testing. Let them ask a question. When you have shown somebody what you made, tap I made it.
You made something! I am so proud that you gave it a go. If you like, you can tell me all about it. Or tap the treat button.
Fantastic work! Which change helped your tower stay up? If you want, you can tell me what you did, or just show a grown-up. You can also go straight to your reward.

Fantastic work! What did you change after your customer tested it? If you want, you can tell me what you did, or just show a grown-up. You can also go straight to your reward.
Fantastic work! Which two ideas did your team use in the rescue? If you want, you can tell me what you did, or just show a grown-up. You can also go straight to your reward.
Fantastic work! What did you learn when someone else tried your maze? If you want, you can tell me what you did, or just show a grown-up. You can also go straight to your reward.
Fantastic work! What stayed the same in your two tests? What changed? If you want, you can tell me what you did, or just show a grown-up. You can also go straight to your reward.
Fantastic work! Which direction did you change to help your partner? If you want, you can tell me what you did, or just show a grown-up. You can also go straight to your reward.
What’s a frog’s favourite drink? ... Croak-a-cola!
What is a lion’s favourite type of music? ... Anything with a good roar-thm!
What do you call a dog magician? ... A labra-cadabra-dor!
What do you call a superhero potato? ... Super Spud!
Why did the crayon win the race? ... It took the colourful shortcut!
What did the pencil say to the paper? ... You’ve got a point!
What does a cloud wear under its raincoat? ... Thunderwear!
What do you call a magic owl? ... Hoo-dini!
Why did the cookie go to the doctor? ... It felt crumby!
Why did the teddy bear say no to cake? ... It was already stuffed!
What do you call a room with no doors or windows? ... A mushroom!
What did Rainbow Rocket say before taking off? ... Ready, steady, rainbow!
What do you call a funny mountain? ... Hill-arious!
What do you call a bear in the rain? ... A drizzly bear!
What did the wall say to the other wall? ... Meet you at the corner!
What do you call a koala who sings? ... A koala-ty performer!
How does the moon get a haircut? ... Eclipse it!
What do cats eat for breakfast? ... Mice crispies!
What do you call cheese that isn’t yours? ... Nacho cheese!
What did the volcano say to its friend? ... I lava you!
What’s a lion’s favourite snack? ... Anything that goes crunch-a-munch!
Why did the orange stop running? ... It ran out of juice!
Why did the lion bring a pencil to the party? ... To draw a crowd!
What do you call a sleeping dinosaur? ... A dino-snore!
What do you call a bee who can’t decide? ... A maybe!
What did the lion say to his new shoes? ... You’re pawsome!
Why did the computer feel cold? ... It left its windows open!
Why did the scarecrow get a medal? ... It was outstanding in its field!
What do lions wear to bed? ... Their roar-jamas!
Why did the pirate learn the alphabet slowly? ... He got stuck at C!
Why did Captain Comet take a sandwich to the moon? ... Because space snacks are out of this world!
What do you call a lion wearing sunglasses? ... A cool cat!
What do you call a monkey with a banana phone? ... A-peeling!
What did the ocean say to the beach? ... Nothing. It just waved!
Why did the superhero bring string? ... To tie up the loose ends!
Why did Lenny sleep under the stars? ... He wanted a million-star hotel!
Why did Lenny bring a map to the kitchen? ... He was hunting for the snack treasure!
Why did the rocket bring a spoon? ... For a taste of the Milky Way!
Why did the bicycle fall over? ... It was two-tired!
Why did the kangaroo become a comedian? ... It had everyone jumping with laughter!
Why did Thunder Paws bring an umbrella? ... There was a chance of paw-shower!
Why did the cow go to space? ... To see the moooon!
What did one plate say to the other? ... Dinner is on me!
Why did the chicken join the band? ... It had the drumsticks!
Why did the cupcake go to school? ... To get a little batter!
How do you make a tissue dance? ... Put a little boogie in it!
What kind of music do planets love? ... Neptunes!
What do you call a sleeping pizza? ... A pi-z-z-z-a!
What do you call a rabbit who tells jokes? ... A funny bunny!
What did the sock say to the shoe? ... I’ve got your back heel!
What did the duck say when it bought a hat? ... Put it on my bill!
What do you call a crocodile detective? ... An investi-gator!
Why did the bee have sticky hair? ... It used a honeycomb!
What do you call a lion who likes building things? ... A roar-chitect!
Why did the duck take a pencil to the pond? ... To draw a quack-ture!
What did Lenny say when the biscuit disappeared? ... Crikey! That was my last crumb!
Why was the lion so good at hide-and-seek? ... Because nobody could find his mane hiding spot!
What do you call a lion with a microphone? ... The king of the sing-along!
Why did the maths book look worried? ... It had too many problems!
What did the emu do at the playground? ... It went down the slide, feet first!
What did the zero say to the eight? ... Nice belt!
What did the star say after its first race? ... I really shone out there!
What did one snowflake say to another? ... You’re one of a kind!
Why did Super Sprout bring a watering can? ... To grow her superpowers!
Why did the banana visit the doctor? ... It wasn’t peeling well!
Why was Lenny late to the picnic? ... He was having a bad mane day!
What kind of tree fits in your hand? ... A palm tree!
Why was the broom late? ... It overswept!
What did the blanket say to the bed? ... I’ve got you covered!
Why did the pirate go to the doctor? ... To get his arrrr checked!
What did the big flower say to the little flower? ... Hi, bud!
What do you call a sleeping bull? ... A bulldozer!
Why did the fish blush? ... Because it saw the ocean’s bottom!
Why did the egg hide behind the curtain? ... It was a little chicken!
How do you organise a space party? ... You planet!
What do you call a bear with no teeth? ... A gummy bear!
Why did the clock get into trouble? ... It kept tocking!
Where does a sheep get its wool cut? ... At the baa-ber!
Where do superheroes eat lunch? ... At the super-market!
What did the left eye say to the right eye? ... Between us, something smells!
